cards.text: Meet Micah the Moreshite. The word of the LORD comes to him in the days of THREE kings of Judah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, and what he sees is about two cities: Samaria and Jerusalem. Three kings, friend! I had ONE kitchen and still got demoted to a drawer.
Micah doesn't ease into this one. No small talk, no 'how was your weekend,' he kicks it off with HEAR! LISTEN! like a phone alarm at 5 a.m. with the volume ALL the way up.

cards.question: Micah opens with a call to listen. Who does he call to hear him?

answers.text: All peoples and the whole earth
The kings and priests of Judah
The elders and prophets of Israel

cards.text: Then Micah says, "May the Lord GOD bear witness against you, the Lord from His holy temple." Witness AGAINST you, friend, and that is NOT a glowing job reference.
And behold, the LORD comes forth from His dwelling place to come down and tread on the high places of the earth. Trust me, friend, nobody's hitting snooze on THAT alarm.

cards.question: When the LORD treads on the high places of the earth, what do the mountains beneath Him do?
While the mountains melt beneath the LORD, the valleys hold firm.

cards.text: So what's all this melting and splitting for? Micah says, "All this is for the transgression of Jacob and the sins of the house of Israel."

cards.question: Micah asks, "What is the transgression of Jacob?" Which city does he point to?
Then Micah asks about the high place of Judah, and the city he names is ___.

cards.text: Now the LORD speaks: He'll make Samaria a heap of rubble in the open field, a planting area for a vineyard, with her stones poured into the valley and her foundations exposed. That's not a remodel, friend, that's the whole house down to the dirt.

cards.question: Along with the city itself, the LORD says He will destroy all of Samaria's ___.

cards.text: ALL her carved images smashed to pieces and ALL her wages burned in the fire, so there's no yard sale after this one, friend. Then the LORD says, "Since she collected the wages of a prostitute, they will be used again on a prostitute."

cards.question: After hearing what's coming for Samaria, Micah says he will lament and wail.

cards.text: Micah says he'll walk barefoot and naked, howl like a jackal and mourn like an ostrich. Me, when I got slid into the junk drawer, I sulked in silence for YEARS, but Micah grieves out loud, and honestly, friend, that's healthier.

cards.question: Micah says Samaria's wound is incurable. How far has it spread?

cards.text: Now Micah's lament goes town by town, like a roll call where nobody wants to hear their name. It starts with this: "Do not tell it in Gath; do not weep at all."

cards.question: Next on Micah's list is Beth-leaphrah. What does he tell its people to do?

cards.text: Then Micah tells the dwellers of Shaphir to depart in shameful nakedness. Friend, I've had some embarrassing exits, getting slid into a junk drawer for one, but at least I kept my apron on.
The dwellers of Zaanan will not come out, like when the doorbell rings and the whole house goes dead silent. And Beth-ezel is in mourning, its support taken away.
The people of Maroth pined for good, like staring at a package tracker that says 'out for delivery' all day long. But calamity came down instead, even to the gate of Jerusalem.

cards.question: The calamity that came down on Maroth came from the LORD.

cards.text: Next up, Lachish, and Micah has a command for it: "Harness your chariot horses, O dweller of Lachish." That's the old-school version of 'go start the car,' friend.

cards.question: Micah calls Lachish the beginning of ___ to the Daughter of Zion.

cards.text: The transgressions of Israel were found in Lachish, and therefore Micah says to send farewell gifts to Moresheth-gath. That's the goodbye card the whole office signs, where everybody writes 'Good luck!' and backs away slowly.

cards.question: Micah says the houses of Achzib will prove dependable to the kings of Israel.
Then comes word for Mareshah. What is coming against Mareshah again?

cards.text: And the glory of Israel will come to Adullam. Then Micah's last call: shave yourselves bald, cut off your hair, and make yourselves as bald as an eagle.

cards.question: Why does Micah tell the people to shave themselves bald?

answers.text: To keep a vow to the LORD

cards.question: Micah says their precious children will go from them into ___.
